subject: MAP & evaluation sprint — defining success criteria and cutover checklist
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@quantomhealth.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & Eval sprint — defining success criteria

Thanks Sean — attaching our MAP template and a short summary of what we need to validate during the pilot. Quick background: we want to run a 4-week evaluation focused on document ingestion + question-answering over our regulatory corpus. Core asks: predictable P95 latency, inference cost estimate at target throughput, and automated evidence for retention/auditability.

Attached: Quantom_MAP_Template.xlsx (MAP draft)

High level asks from Quantom: 
- Success: model answers match SME adjudication > 90% on concordance set (n=250)
- Exit gate: no P1 production-impacting regressions during canary (latency P95 under 500ms, 99.9% availability window)
- Acceptance tests: sample QA suite, integration smoke with SSO + VPC peering, and audit log shipping to our Splunk instance

Can you and your team sketch acceptance tests and a simple cutover checklist we can sign? Also need an estimated cost delta if we enable KV caching and int8 quantization.

—Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Integrations, Quantom Health
From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@quantomhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & Eval sprint — defining success criteria

Sara — thanks for the clear brief and the template. I reviewed the MAP and sketched a concise acceptance-runbook that maps directly to the three buckets you called out. I attached a short test script + a draft MAP with roles/owners. Key points below so we can align before you finalize: 

1) Acceptance criteria (proposal)
- Functional concordance: adjudication concordance >= 92% on a blinded holdout (n=250)
- Latency & availability: P95 < 450ms (at expected concurrency), 99.9% availability for canary window
- Error tolerance: inference error rate (5xx/timeout) < 0.5% during sampling windows
- Cost guardrail: incremental token cost <= 30% above baseline inference (we’ll provide estimate with caching/quantization knobs)

2) Exit gates (hard stops)
- Blocker: any data-exfil incident or evidence not forwarded to your Splunk instance within the agreed window
- Blocker: concordance < 85% after model tuning round
- Operational: repeated autoscaling instability (unrecoverable thrash) during two consecutive day windows

3) Acceptance tests (examples we’ll run during weeks 1–3)
- Integration smoke: ingestion pipeline (S3 -> Redwood) + SSO sign-in test (okta)
- Functional: 250-case concordance run (blinded) with SME adjudication
- Performance: synthetic concurrency ramp to projected QPS, capture latency P50/P95/P99, and token-level cost sampling
- Observability: verify audit log delivery to Splunk + proof-of-keystore rotation recorded in KMS logs

Next steps: 
- I’ll share Redwood_Eval_Test_Scripts_v1.pdf and a mutual-action-plan-draft.docx. Ben — can you estimate cost delta for: (a) baseline, (b) with prefix caching, (c) with int8 quantization? We’ll put numbers into the MAP and return for Sara’s legal signoff.

If that looks good Sara, we can schedule a 30-min alignment call tomorrow to lock owners and dates.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_Eval_Test_Scripts_v1.pdf; mutual-action-plan-draft.docx
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: QHE acceptance thresholds & risk notes (do not forward)

Internal quick note on thresholds & operational controls before we push numbers to Quantom: 
- Concordance threshold: target 92% pass / acceptance; contingency tuning sprint if 88–91%
- Latency target: P95 < 450ms at expected concurrency (we should guarantee canary pool size and a fallback variant pinned to a smaller context length)
- Error budget: 0.5% inference errors per 24h window; anything above requires incident review
- Data security: require SOC2 evidence + one week of audit-log retention in their Splunk instance for the pilot period; encryption-in-transit and at-rest mandatory
- Cutover checklist (short):
  - Owner signoff (Quantom product lead)
  - Successful 250-case concordance run with SME notes attached
  - Latency run within guardrail for 3 sampling windows
  - Audit logs validated and indexed by Quantom Splunk team

Risks: 
- If the concordance sits in the 86–88% band after tuning sprint, prepare rollback plan to baseline model (no caching, full context) and we ask Quantom to extend pilot 1 week for additional tuning.

Ben — can you validate the cost delta matrix and add a recommended default (we usually propose caching + int8 for cost-sensitive customers). I’ll incorporate language for the exit gates and the DocuSign flow.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean and Marissa — this is very helpful and aligns with our internal priorities. We reviewed the draft MAP and Redwood’s proposed acceptance tests. A few confirmations from our side before DocuSign: 
- Concordance: we can accept the 92% target for sign-off; if results fall in 88–91% we’ll authorize a single 5-business-day tuning sprint (as you described) before invoking rollback
- Latency & error budget: P95 < 450ms and error rate < 0.5% accepted for canary
- Security: SOC2 + audit-log delivery to Splunk (indexing confirmation required)
- Cost: please include the three-column cost delta table in the MAP (baseline / caching / caching+int8) so our procurement team can run TCO analysis

Attached: signed cover sheet (we’ll sign full MAP via DocuSign once Redwood adds the cost table and owner names). Please send the DocuSign link and we’ll pick a start date (target week of Nov 22).
